name: Nonlinear Direct Measures and the Residual Method Catalog
description: Classifies seven nonlinear residual families with dominance data blocking orientation. The 25-row inventory is terminally classified but not universally closed.

program.name: The Termination Axis
program.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

oneLine: Every nonlinear residual family carries its row-specific support and the twenty-five-row inventory is terminally classified without being universally closed.
summary: The theory splits the unrestricted direct residue into seven nonlinear families with an assigned five-tag status table. The questions are the global orientation of the system by direct measures and the extra data that closes the transparent bounded-degree row. With supplied eventual base dominance or a member of the concrete dominance class TransparentDominanceWitnessClass, a transparent bounded polynomial with unbounded range is blocked by the existing polynomial barrier, while the boundary alone carries the recorded status projection-required. The cross-term quadratic, multilinear, WPO-polynomial and max-plus rows are recorded as blocked and supported by their barrier theorems under the premises stated there, the cross-coupled row is recorded as a W1 licensed escape, and the arbitrary-relation row holds for every trace relation because the law carrier admits only the kernel relation by definition, and that relation has the W1 imported-whole escape. A law that keeps both wrapper arguments at a fixed cost and bounds one counter step by a fixed gain cannot orient the duplicating step, and on free terms a measure dropping the wrapper clause and a cross-coupled measure dropping the counter clause each orient it. All twenty-five cross-family rows are packaged with universal support and terminal statuses into a certificate, and the recorded blocked and licensed-escape rows make the inventory not universally closed.
boundary: With eventual base dominance or a member of the concrete dominance class supplied, a transparent bounded polynomial with unbounded range cannot globally orient; without that data the boundary keeps the recorded status projection-required. A direct law that keeps both wrapper arguments and bounds the counter gain cannot orient the duplicating step, and on free terms dropping either clause admits an orienter. The twenty-five-row certificate gives every row support and a terminal recorded status, and the recorded blocked and licensed-escape rows make the inventory not universally closed; the arbitrary-relation dichotomy is complete only because its carrier admits the kernel relation alone.

conclusions.statement: Every row of the twenty-five-row inventory belongs to the ordered list, is supported by its owning-module proposition, and has a terminal status among the five tags, packaged in a certificate with row count, nodup, universal support and universal terminal status.
Some inventoried row carries the recorded status blocked or licensed escape, and not every row carries the recorded status closedByLeanTheorem.

For every nonlinear residual family its row-specific support payload holds, every family belongs to the declared lists with its support, and the status plus projection catalogs package into a boundary certificate with projections.

The transparent-polynomial family carries its row-specific support payload, recorded as requiring existing-theorem projection and closed by the concrete dominance-witness class with its catalogs and universal witness-class barrier.

Each of the bounded cross-term quadratic, bounded multilinear, WPO-polynomial-branch and max-plus direct-fragment families carries its row-specific support payload recording blocking by the existing theorem.

The cross-coupled family carries licensed-escape support with W1 route, global-polynomial class and permitted import, while the unconstrained family carries exact-law-carrier support with the split catalog and law boundary for all relations.

Given any transparent projection boundary and a witness-class member for its measure, its evaluation does not globally orient; this holds for every boundary pointwise and for every dominance criterion through its stored witness, collected with status equality and dominance data in the conditional catalog.

Given full projection data its measure evaluation does not globally orient by the bounded polynomial barrier, and given a boundary with matching data, and in particular any boundary carrying dominance data or in the concrete witness class, its evaluation does not globally orient, while the boundary alone satisfies only the boundary-only catalog and stays projection-required.

For every trace relation, either it has a non-W0 licensed escape or the law carrier, admitting only the kernel relation by definition, contains no direct first-order method for it; the kernel relation has the W1 imported-whole escape, and the direct law is backed by an additive measure for the linear benchmark member.

For any unconstrained direct law it is false that its evaluation strictly increases on the duplicating step for all base, seed and counter values, and hence no law evaluation globally orients the system; the same holds through any comparison tracked by less-than, and every additive measure satisfies the exact law with no extra premise.

Dropping the wrapper clause, the botRightWeight measure forgets its right argument and strictly orients the step; dropping the counter-gain clause, the cross-coupled witness keeps both wrapper arguments, orients the step and admits no fixed counter gain.

The transparent-with-dominance row is supported by the dominance-criteria catalog, the cross-coupled row by the existing W1 witness and import permission, and the arbitrary-relation row by the method-law dichotomy for all relations; every local constructor belongs to the list with its support, packaged with the parent status into a certificate.

The seven families and five statuses form finite duplicate-free lists with membership characterizations, and every family has a listed status realizing the finite assigned-status catalog by case analysis.

The thirty-five-row ledger with ten matrix rows followed by twenty-five cross-family rows is consistent by membership and decidable status projection, and contains rows with each recorded status: closed, conditional, adapter-only and open.

The three-edge canonical reduction graph is acyclic with no self-loops or two-cycles because every canonical target is never a canonical source, so no path returns to its start and reduction meets coverage to the weaker status.

openPoints: Blocking for the transparent polynomial row requires a supplied dominance witness: the boundary alone stays projection-required and does not derive dominance.
Cross-term, multilinear, WPO and max-plus blocking holds only under the stated unbounded-range hypotheses plus base boundedness, base dominance or eventual dominance as applicable.
The cross-coupled witness is a licensed W1 escape that needs a permitted import; it does not give internal closure.

The law carrier is deliberately finite and anchored to the kernel relation; off that relation the dichotomy holds as vacuous emptiness and the split catalog does not classify any external unconstrained method domain.

The twenty-five-row inventory is terminally classified with universal support but explicitly not universally closed, witnessed by blocked and licensed-escape rows; the thirty-five-row ledger likewise records closed, conditional, adapter-only and open outcomes with no blanket closure.
Reduction can only weaken coverage to the meet of source and target, and canonical targets are never reused as sources, so walks terminate without cycles.

subTopics.name: Residual closure inventory, ledger and graph

files.summary: This module defines row-specific support payloads for seven nonlinear residual families, combining statuses, finite catalogs, hypothesis-exact barriers, a licensed W1 escape and an exact law-carrier row. It proves each row is supported by its imported barrier or witness and assembles case analysis into a finite projection catalog. It packages status and projection catalogs into a boundary certificate with projections.
files.conclusion: Every nonlinear residual family carries its row-specific support payload, yielding a complete projection catalog and certificate.

files.summary: This module defines transparent dominance criteria pairing a projection boundary with a witness-class assumption. It upgrades criteria to full projection data and shows forgetting dominance recovers the boundary. It proves witness-supplied boundaries carry dominance data and are blocked, collected in a conditional catalog with an alias.
files.conclusion: Every dominance criterion supplies dominance data and blocks global orientation, collected in a conditional catalog.

files.summary: This module defines three concrete dominance witnesses for bounded polynomial measures: trivial monomial, wrap-dominant affine and successor identity. It proves each implies eventual dominance at the base, with the trivial case as a wrapper around successor identity. It unions them into a transparent witness class whose every member yields eventual dominance.
files.conclusion: Each branch of the transparent dominance witness class implies eventual dominance at the base.

files.summary: This module defines nonlinear relations, a two-law vocabulary with W0 and W1 routes, licensed-escape payloads and finite law carriers anchored to Step. It proves the direct and imported-whole laws are backed by existing witnesses and builds canonical carriers. It proves every relation satisfies a dichotomy between a licensed non-W0 escape and absence of a direct W0 method, packaged as an exact boundary.
files.conclusion: Every nonlinear relation is classified as either having the licensed W1 escape or having no direct first-order method in the carrier.

files.summary: This module introduces seven nonlinear residual families and their status vocabulary with finite family and status lists. It defines the family-to-status assignment and proves exact table equations and membership characterizations. It shows every family has a listed status and realizes the finite assigned-status catalog.
files.conclusion: The seven nonlinear residual families and five statuses form duplicate-free finite lists with a realized assignment catalog.

files.summary: This module separates a transparent bounded-degree boundary carrying transparency and unboundedness from stronger data adding eventual dominance. It shows data implies dominance-data status and that the row remains projection-required. It proves boundaries with supplied data or witness-class members are blocked by the existing polynomial barrier and packages a boundary-only catalog.
files.conclusion: Boundaries with supplied dominance data or witness-class membership are blocked, while the boundary alone remains projection-required.

files.summary: This module states an exact unconstrained law of wrapper argument retention plus bounded counter gain and proves it blocks the duplicating step without linearity or range hypotheses. It shows every additive measure satisfies the law and proves both clauses load-bearing via botRightWeight and cross-coupled escapes. It compiles the carrier dichotomy off Step as vacuous emptiness and notes the bounded tropical escape.
files.conclusion: The exact wrapper-retention plus bounded-counter-gain law blocks the duplicating step with both clauses load-bearing.

files.summary: This module defines a three-tag subdivision of the unconstrained row with statuses and support propositions for dominance-blocked, licensed-escape and law-dichotomy cases. It proves membership characterizations and that each constructor has its selected support, with non-overclaim inequalities. It assembles the local split catalog and certificate projecting parent status and catalog, explicitly without an external-domain classifier.
files.conclusion: The three local rows each carry their selected support, yielding a complete split catalog and certificate.

files.summary: This file closes a twenty-five-row cross-family residual inventory with theorem-backed support per row. It assigns source families and five terminal statuses with no open constructors. It proves exact length, nodup, support, terminal status, and an explicit non-overclaim boundary separating terminal classification from universal closure. It packages these as a universal completion certificate.
files.conclusion: The twenty-five-row residual inventory is terminally classified with universal support but explicitly not universally closed.

files.summary: This file unifies matrix and cross-family residual rows under a four-element coverage vocabulary. It defines mappings from upstream matrix and RMCC statuses to closed, conditional, adapter-only, and open. It lists thirty-five ledger rows and proves consistency of membership and projected status by decidable computation. It exhibits rows of each of the four kinds with no blanket closure.
files.conclusion: The thirty-five-row residual ledger is consistent with upstream matrix and cross-family status functions and contains each status kind.

files.summary: This file adds typed cross-family reduction edges over the residual ledger. It defines a meet operation on coverage statuses and three canonical edges with proof anchors. It defines paths and cycles and proves the canonical graph acyclic with no self-loops or two-cycles because targets are never sources. It defines meet-closure under one reduction step with a weakening law.
files.conclusion: The three-edge canonical reduction graph is acyclic with meet-weakening status closure.

files.summary: The file provides a thin stable import boundary that aliases residual-method closure rows, statuses, catalog surfaces, and certificates for residual, matrix-residual, FBI, generic-DP, semantic, nonlinear-direct, and W1 families. It defines entrypoint theorems that re-expose the underlying catalog certificates and universal support and terminal-status claims without duplicating proof content. Projection abbreviations expose the passage from each certificate to its catalog and status witnesses.
files.conclusion: The file exposes stable certificates for residual, matrix, FBI, generic-DP, semantic, nonlinear and W1 boundaries without adding new proofs.

files.summary: The file checks the nonlinear direct-boundary catalog: residual families and statuses with completeness and nodup lemmas, the status catalog, supported predicates, projection-boundary and dominance and closure catalogs, blocked families, licensed escape and exact-law witnesses, and unconstrained-split and projection certificates. Twelve examples exhibit families, prove status equalities by rfl, exhibit supported instances and catalogs, and project split and boundary certificates.
files.conclusion: The residual catalog is complete with blocked, projection-requiring, licensed-escape and exact-law statuses and supported certificates for the latter three.

files.summary: The file checks transparent-polynomial dominance criteria: projection boundaries and data, dominance-data existence, criteria with boundary preservation, status, dominance-data production and row closure, plus dominance and closure catalogs. Seven examples coerce a criterion to projection data, prove boundary preservation, required-projection status, dominance-data production and row closure, and exhibit the catalogs.
files.conclusion: Every transparent-polynomial dominance criterion supplies dominance data and closes its transparent row.

files.summary: The file checks the nonlinear method-law carrier: relations, method laws, routes with exactness, licensed escapes, law carriers with direct and imported support and carriers, step equalities, escape and first-order-method existence, projections, dichotomy and no-method-or-escape disjunction, unconditional support and exact-boundary claims, with axiom closure for each. Five examples prove route equalities, licensed escape, the boundary disjunction at Step, and unconditional support.
files.conclusion: Arbitrary relations obey an exact law dichotomy with unconditional support for the boundary row.

files.summary: The file checks transparent-polynomial projection: boundaries, data, dominance-data existence, requirements that force projection status, bounded-polynomial barriers, blocked theorems with data or witness classes, dominance witnesses with base domination, unconditional dominance theorems, residual statuses and vector-order notions. Fourteen examples prove required-projection status, status-list length and membership, transparency and unboundedness projections, data-to-boundary conversion, dominance-data production and barrier theorems with data, witness classes and unconditional variants, and exhibit the boundary catalog.
files.conclusion: Transparent-polynomial projection boundaries with dominance witnesses unconditionally block global orientation.

files.summary: The file checks the unconstrained split: rows and statuses with row lists, status functions, supported predicates, nodup, length and completeness lemmas, listed-status and per-row support and non-membership lemmas, and split catalogs and certificates with projections. Seven examples exhibit rows, prove status equalities by rfl, prove licensed-escape support, and project parent status and split catalog from the split certificate.
files.conclusion: The unconstrained split catalog exactly covers its three rows with their stated statuses.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the residual-method API and its certificates. It runs #check for closure, matrix, FBI, generic-DP, semantic, nonlinear and W1 certificates with their projections, plus root reachability #checks for the polynomial payload observer and escape family. Examples exhibit each certificate and the universal support and terminality over all rows.
files.conclusion: All residual-method rows are supported and terminal while orientation requires the escape pump.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the residual-method closure catalog. It runs paired #check and #print axioms for sources, statuses, rows, support, nodup, length, completeness, terminality and certificate projections. Examples exercise the live surface, decide membership, check source and status values, derive support for five rows, and witness blocked and licensed-escape statuses with non-universal closure.
files.conclusion: The catalog is complete and terminal but exhibits blocked and licensed-escape witnesses against universal closure.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the residual-method ledger. It runs #check and #print axioms for coverage statuses, family mappings, row lists, nodup, length and consistency with closed, open, adapter-only and conditional witnesses. Examples exhibit each of the four statuses, canonical per-family values, and the 35-row count.
files.conclusion: The 35-row ledger is consistent and attests all four coverage statuses.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the residual reduction graph. It runs #check for status meet, commutativity, idempotence, absorption, canonical edges and acyclicity with reduction and meet monotonicity. Examples instantiate acyclicity, no self-loops, no two-cycles, the three-edge count, meet values, commutativity and idempotence.
files.conclusion: The canonical reduction graph is acyclic with three edges and a well-behaved status meet.

claims.heading: Thm. 4.4
claims.reason: The structure packages wrapper retention and bounded counter gain, and the three theorems refute orientation for the measure itself, for any tracked relation forcing less-than, and for the global system relation.
